newsitem.title: GERMANY: Telekom says keeping capital increase right.
newsitem.headline: Telekom says keeping capital increase right.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG said on Tuesday it would keep its right to a capital increase if the German government goes ahead with a plan to sell its share in the phone company.
Telekom spokesman Ulrich Lissek also said Telekom would not lose sight of shareholders' interests.
Lissek said Telekom was in close talks with the Finance Ministry, but declined to specify what the two sides were discussing.
Government sources told Reuters on Tuesday that Bonn was considering selling 287 million shares in Telekom in 1997 to help close a gaping budget deficit.
Bonn was also considering selling its remaining stake in Telekom by the end of 1998, the sources said.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel has said he wanted to narrow the budget gap by selling Telekom shares. Under its privatisation plan, Telekom was expected to sell additional shares as part of a capital increase by the year 2000.
